_readme: What this file is: the record of what Google Cloud holds for this app,
measured from this repository and from the console itself on 2026-11-02.
tool/check_google_sign_in_config.dart reads it, and
test/auth_google_sign_in_configuration_test.dart fails while it says the
registration is missing.
It contains no secret. A client id and a SHA-1 certificate fingerprint are
public identifiers: the client id is compiled into the APK and the
fingerprint is meant to be pasted into the Google console.
The two Google Cloud projects are deliberately different. 644544428760
(new-coffee-4d196) is the Firebase project that google-services.json and
lib/firebase_options.dart are generated from - it owns Cloud Messaging.
496541472556 (project ID new-coffee-512019) owns the OAuth web client that
Supabase redirects to and the two Android clients below, so it is the only
project where an Android OAuth client can be registered. Nothing in
android/ or lib/ reads default_web_client_id, which is why the login does
not need google-services.json at all; the checker verifies that every build.
What was wrong, in the order it was found (all measured, none guessed):
1. Both OAuth projects were in scheduled deletion, so every client id
under them was dead. Restored 2026-11-02; deletion was cancelled, not
a single client deleted.
2. The Android client that already existed registered package
'com.example.new_cofee' - one 'f' short of android/app/build.gradle.kts
applicationId 'com.example.new_coffee'. Credential Manager cannot match
a package it was never told, and says '[16] Account reauth failed'.
The package name is now corrected in the console.
3. The consent screen is External + Testing, so only listed test users can
sign in. The account on the test device is added as a test user.
4. With 1-3 fixed, Google issued an ID token and Supabase still refused it:
'nonces mismatch'. See the nonce note under evidence - the app stopped
sending a client nonce because this path can never satisfy one.
Re-check the fingerprints after any keystore change with
./gradlew :app:printSigningFingerprints
which compares them with this file and says MATCHES or DOES NOT MATCH. A
stale SHA-1 here is the same dead end as a missing one, for one build type
only, which is the hardest kind to notice.
Do not change the web client Supabase is configured with, and do not create
a third project for this.

consentScreen.note: A release build signing in with an account that is not a test user is refused by the consent screen, not by the client registration. Publishing the app to 'In production' is the step that removes the cap, and it needs the ownership verification the console asks for.

evidence: GET https://webzzasosevzymftgszn.supabase.co/auth/v1/authorize?provider=google
-> 302 accounts.google.com/o/oauth2/v2/auth?client_id=<webClientId above>
-> redirect_uri=<redirectUriRegisteredOnWebClient above>, scope=email profile
GET that authorize URL with no cookies -> Google accepts the client and
continues to the consent flow (requestPath=/signin/oauth/v3/consent, no
authError). The same request with one digit of the client id changed ->
invalid_client. So the web client exists and its Supabase callback is
registered.
emulator-5554, 2026-11-02 00:36, debug APK built from this branch:
Auth.Api.Credentials: cxqz: [16] Account reauth failed.
That was the misspelled package name in the console. After the fix the
same device logged the flow through:
11-02 12:18:46.563 I/Auth.Api.Credentials:
[FetchGoogleIdTokenCredentialOperation] Operation succeeded
with no AuthException afterwards.
The nonce finding, because it is the part a future reader will want to
undo: GoogleSignIn.initialize(nonce:) reaches Credential Manager (the plugin
sets it on GetSignInWithGoogleOption) but the ID token that comes back
carries Google's own nonce, not SHA-256 of the one sent. Measured on
emulator-5554 at 09:13Z on 2026-11-02: token iat one second before the
exchange, token nonce claim 6f4f02d1.., SHA-256 of the local nonce 7c7d8ba1..,
and GoTrue answered AuthException: nonces mismatch. A client nonce on this
path is unsatisfiable, so the app sends none - which is also what Supabase's
own native Flutter sample does. The token is still bound to this app by its
aud (the web client id) and by Google's signature.
2026-11-02: the release Android client above was created from the SHA-1 that
./gradlew :app:printSigningFingerprints printed in the same session
('release SHA-1 MATCHES google_sign_in_setup.json'). It is registered, not
yet proven: no release-signed build has completed a sign-in on a device, and
the account used so far is a test user on a Testing consent screen.
